Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the players of Australia. It will be Saim Ayub and Abdullah Shafique to open the innings for Pakistan. Mitchell Starc will get proceedings underway with the ball. Let's go...
... The Run Chase ...

Heading into the second innings, Australia must bowl with precision to counter Pakistan’s capable batting lineup. Adelaide Oval’s pitch has offered some assistance to both pace and spin, which Australia’s experienced bowlers will look to capitalize on and take early wickets. 164 is a modest target and Pakistan should level up the series but will need to be positive with the bat. Let's see how the run chase pans out. Join us in a bit to find out.

Pakistan's bowling attack was spearheaded by Haris Rauf, who had an outstanding performance, taking 5 wickets for just 29 runs in his 8 overs. Shaheen Afridi and Mohammad Hasnain also made important contributions, claiming 3 and 1 wicket individually. Naseem Shah also chipped in with 1 wicket but was on the expensive side, finishing with 1/65 in his quota of 10 overs. The collective effort from Pakistan's bowlers was crucial in stifling Australia's scoring rate and reducing them to a low total.

Pakistan's bowlers dominated, keeping Australia under pressure throughout. As for Australia's batting, the most significant contributions came from Steven Smith, who top-scored with 35 runs off 48 balls. Josh Inglis and Matthew Short added 18 runs, and 19 runs respectively but their stays at the crease were brief. Glenn Maxwell (16 off 21) and Aaron Hardie (14 off 29) tried to fight back, but both were dismissed cheaply, leaving captain Pat Cummins a lot to do. Adam Zampa did play a handy knock to get them over the 150-run mark. The middle and lower order failed to get going, leading to Australia's downfall. The team never seemed to settle, with Pakistan's bowlers consistently finding the right lengths and keeping Australia under control.

Outstanding from Pakistan! Their bowlers have done half their job and they are in pole position to level the series. Australia have been outplayed here in the first innings and have been bowled out with a fair chunk of overs to go. They found themselves in a difficult position after being put into bat. They were bowled out for 163 just in 35 overs, largely due to disciplined bowling from Pakistan. Australia began solidly but were unable to build any substantial partnerships, falling victim to regular wickets.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set for the 2nd ODI to get underway! The umpires are making their way out to the middle followed by the opening pair of Australia - Matthew Short and Jake Fraser-McGurk. Pakistan almost managed a staggering comeback in the first ODI and the pacers really rose to the occasion but they just didn't have enough runs on the board and that batting line-up really needs to fire if they are to level the series here in Adelaide.

Hello and a warm welcome to one and all. It is time for the 2nd ODI between Australia and Pakistan to get underway in Adelaide and with the series on the line, it is a must win game for the visitors whereas the hosts will look to wrap things up before a few of their big guns are rested for the final ODI.
... MATCH DAY ...

After edging Pakistan in a thrilling low-scoring contest, Australia targets a series-clinching win in the second ODI. Pakistan, determined to stay alive in the series, seeks an upset victory over the World Champions at Adelaide Oval. Both sides would be looking to put up a better batting display as runs were hard to come by in the series opener, with neither Australia nor Pakistan producing a single half-centurion in the first ODI. Australia, buoyed by the match-winning performance from skipper Pat Cummins, will look to consolidate their lead. Despite restricting the opposition to a low score, Australia's batting unit struggled to seal the deal, relying on the clutch inning from skipper Pat Cummins. Matthew Short and Jake Fraser-McGurk will look to rectify this with a solid start, aided by the top-notch firepower of Steven Smith, Josh Inglis, Marnus Labuschagne and Glenn Maxwell down the order. Australia may also consider introducing youngster Cooper Connolly, whose all-round abilities and left-arm spin could complement Zampa's leg-spin against Pakistan's predominantly right-handed batting lineup. In the series opener, Pakistan showed heart but failed to defend a subpar total against the World Champions. The Asian side, led by Mohammad Rizwan, seeks a batting resurgence in the second ODI, counting on Babar Azam, Mohammad Rizwan, Abdullah Shafique and Saim Ayub to deliver match-winning performances. The Asian side may also inject freshness in their line-up with the addition of Arafat Minhas, Aamer Jamal, or even Faisal Akram, giving them abundant all-round options. Will Pakistan bounce back to level the series, or will Australia get an unassailable lead in this 3-match ODI series? We will get our answer soon. We can expect another thrilling contest in the second ODI.
